patient_trials_check.note: Pi-Sunyer 2015 PMID 26132939; 8.4 kg on 106.2 kg baseline = 7.9%.

magnitude_check.finding: No primary source states a rodent-vs-human weight-loss magnitude comparison. Lau 2015 full text inaccessible (abstract has none). Gabery 2020 gives both sides in one paper but never compares them: intro 'up to twice as much in patients with obesity, approaching 15 kg'; results DIO mice 22% (100 nmol/kg, 3 wk), 17-18% (9.7 nmol/kg, 11 d), 10% (1 nmol/kg); its only stated human matches are food preference and an energy-expenditure extrapolation. Knudsen & Lau 2019 is a review and not usable.
magnitude_check.computed_bin: within_2x on percent-of-baseline loss (rodent 15-22% in 10-21 days vs human 7.9% at 56 wk / 14.9% at 68 wk); dose per kg is >=10x higher and duration 10-20x shorter in rodents, so 'at matched exposure' is unsupported either way.
magnitude_check.recommendation: Keep direction_only if magnitude must come from the source's own comparison; set within_2x only if the atlas defines magnitude as a checker-computed bin from the two primary numbers (see rule_questions).

missing: Safety, 2014, candidate contra: FDA Saxenda Pharmacology Review NDA 206321 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2014/206321Orig1s000PharmR.pdf, Reference ID 3627306) puts tox-species silence beside the weight-management clinic: 'In repeat dose toxicity studies, up to 5 mg/kg/day liraglutide had no effect on gall bladder of mice treated for up to 13 weeks or cynomolgus monkeys treated for up to 52 weeks.' vs 'Increased incidences of cholelithiasis and cholecystitis were noted in liraglutide-treated subjects in clinical studies of >1.8 mg/day liraglutide for weight management, but not in clinical studies of <1.8 mg/day liraglutide for the treatment of T2DM.' Also heart rate: 'absence of an effect of liraglutide on heart rate in monkeys, it is unclear if GLP-1Rs in the sino-atrial node mediate the effects of liraglutide on heart rate in humans.' Model = repeat-dose tox species (mouse/monkey); population = obesity (>1.8 mg); comparison_stated = true; model_filed = true. Under the safety definition ('or its silence') this is a silence that did not hold.

model_filed: the same review names DIO Sprague Dawley rats, candy-fed DIO rats, DIO C57 mice, MSG-lesioned Wistar rats, Gottingen minipigs and rhesus monkeys for liraglutide weight management; the draft's model_filed nulls can be set true for engagement, dose and efficacy. The draft said this review was not retrievable; it is (curl + pdftotext).

Optional engagement entry, 2020, same: Gabery 2020 (10.1172/jci.insight.133429) 'These results are in accordance with observations in humans where reward and food preference were altered in response to GLP-1RA treatment, including semaglutide' (verbatim, Discussion); product_in_model true (semaglutide), model DIO mouse/rat. Status unchanged, so not required.
rule_questions: Does a citation-backed cross-species sentence in a primary paper's limitations/introduction ('lowers body weight in ... rats, obese pigs, and humans') count as 'a published comparison', or must the source compare its own model result with a patient result? I applied the strict reading (untested).

Can a retrodiction (model reproduces a clinical pattern already published) earn same? The brief's wording ('model's prediction agreed with patient results') and rule 5 (year of the comparison) do not bar it; suggest a retrodiction: true fact field rather than a status rule.

Does a comparison whose patient side is a sibling population (T2D at 1.2-1.8 mg) count for the non-diabetic obesity context? The context definition says validity belongs to the context, so I demoted to untested; if class-level safety borrowing is allowed, safety reverts to same 2012 with population_match: false.
Is magnitude the source's stated bin or a checker-computed bin from the two primary numbers? If computed, efficacy magnitude is within_2x (percent of baseline), not direction_only.

Does tox-species silence on an adverse event that later appeared in the weight-management trials (cholelithiasis, heart rate) count as contra for safety? The safety definition includes 'or its silence', which would make the 2014 FDA review a contra entry.
